svg.text: Designed for use · the keyboard is its own lid (Polaroid SX-70)
Play: the key module snaps to the body's front face (magnets + 6 pogo pins, MIDI-UART).
Carry: lift it, flip it, lay it face-up on the body — keys on top, panel sealed under it.
Flat panel, no hinge, no cable. Same panel PCB as CASE.
Look shown: Desk — smoked acrylic stack, black panel, gold rules, green cutoff
Hand-lettered legends, wordmark and grille are PLACEHOLDERS — the owner draws or paints the real ones.
PLAYING — top view, real proportions (1 mm = 7 px)
Panel sunk 18 mm in the body rim; caps top out level with the rim.
Gold = pogo pins on the body's front face (flat ENIG pads on the module).
SIDE — carry (module flipped face-up on top)
Keys ride on top, inside a rim 2 mm proud of the black keys:
nothing flat can press them. Lid magnets at the ends → it sleeps.
